notes: Player-facing How to Play text for the combat prototype. Describes the prototype rules, not Captain's Log.
title: How to Play

sections.heading: Goal
lines: Defeat all four Klingons. You lose if your whole party is Defeated.

sections.heading: Tasks
lines: Every task uses one Attribute and one Department from the character's sheet. Attribute + Department = Target Number (TN). Example: Control 10 + Engineering 4 = TN 14.
Roll two d20 (more if you buy bonus dice). Each die that rolls at or under the TN scores a success.
The Difficulty is how many successes you need. TN and Difficulty are separate: TN 14 at Difficulty 2 means each die rolling 14 or lower scores a success, and you need 2 of them.

A Focus that fits the task makes low rolls count as 2 successes: any roll from 1 up to the Department's rating (Engineering 5: a roll of 1-5). Without a Focus only a natural 1 does. A roll of 20 causes a complication.

Different characters have different chances at the same task, because their Attributes, Departments and Focuses differ. The game highlights the strongest choice on the party bar with BEST CHOICE and their TN; it is only advice, and anyone able can still attempt the task.

The buttons around a character show the short version (for example Control + Security, TN 13 · D2); the Task panel explains every number: the Difficulty and what changed it, the Focus, the dice and the cost of bonus dice. After the roll it shows what each die scored and the result.

sections.heading: Stress, Injuries and Defeat
lines: There are no hit points. A successful attack inflicts an Injury: Stun or Deadly (the weapon's setting), with a Severity from the weapon, reduced by the target's Protection (armour; a Klingon's species ability Brak'lul gives 1), never below 1.

Your characters have Stress (STRESS x/y on the party bar and over their heads): the maximum is their Fitness (some talents and species change it). When one of them is hit, you choose: Avoid Injury takes Stress equal to the Severity and they keep fighting, or Accept Injury and they are Defeated. Without enough Stress left, avoiding fills the track and adds a complication.
At maximum Stress a character is Fatigued: +1 Difficulty on every task, no more Stress (so no more Avoid Injury), and you choose one attribute to shut down: tasks using it automatically fail.

A Defeated character falls and can't act. First Aid revives them (they keep the Injury). A Stun Injury wears off at the end of their next turn after they are back on their feet; a Deadly Injury stays, and a Defeated character with a Deadly Injury is Dying.

The Klingon Warriors follow the same rules as your characters: Stress equal to their Fitness (10), shown on their card when you target them. They avoid Injuries with Stress while they can, so it takes several hits to bring one down.

sections.heading: Turns
lines: The portraits at the top show the turn order. The large yellow one is acting now.

The deck is bigger than the screen: use W A S D (or the arrow keys), hold the right mouse button and drag, or on a touch screen drag with one finger, to look around. Scroll the mouse wheel to zoom in and out. The view moves to whoever is acting; press Camera: Follow (top right) to switch to Camera: Free and keep the view where you put it.
Your party acts first each round, then the Klingons take their turns automatically.

Ambush (optional, until anyone attacks): your party member with the best Control + Security can ambush one Klingon they could shoot (in weapon range, with a clear line of fire). Sneak into position first, over several rounds if needed, then on a party turn press Ambush under the hint, click the Klingon, then Ambush (free). They roll at Difficulty 1 (Camouflage or Ambush Tactics gives a free reroll). Success is an automatic hit on that Klingon (an Injury from their weapon, on Stun). Failure means you are spotted: a new round starts at once and the Klingons act first for the rest of the fight. Any attack, by either side, ends the chance.

The arrow at each figure's feet shows which way it is facing: blue for your party, red for Klingons, yellow for whoever is acting, grey once a turn is done. Figures turn toward where they walk and whom they shoot. Facing is for show only and has no effect on the rules.

During the party's turn, click any party member marked Ready in the bar at the bottom (or click them on the map, then Switch) to act with them. You can switch at any time and come back to finish their actions. Each character has one Major and one Minor action (the M and m lights above them); once both are used the turn passes to the next Ready member automatically, and once the whole party is done the Klingons act.

sections.heading: Your turn
lines: Each turn you have one Major action (Attack, Sprint, Assist, Guard, First Aid, Direct, or a task on an object) and one Minor action (Move, Aim, or a simple object interaction), in either order. You can't attack twice.

Click a Klingon to show buttons around it: Stun and Deadly fire at it straight away, Aim sets up a reroll, and Info shows its condition, the Severity a hit would inflict, cover and your chance to hit. Click a party member for Assist (and Switch to hand them the turn). Point at the character who is acting (or tap them) to show their own actions around them; First Aid, Direct, Interact, Extra Minor and Second Major appear only when there is someone to treat, you are in authority, an object is in reach, or you can pay for the extra action. Click the same figure again, or the floor, to put the buttons away.

Guard (Major): Insight + Security at Difficulty 0; attacks against you get +1 Difficulty until the start of your next turn. Guard an ally within one tile instead at Difficulty 1. A gold G marks a guarded figure.

First Aid (Major): Daring + Medicine on an ally within one tile. Revive = Difficulty 2: a Defeated ally is back on their feet (the Injury stays). Treat Injury = Difficulty equal to its Severity: no penalty from it any more, but it is still an Injury.

Direct (Major, 1 Momentum): only the character in authority (a nominated leader, else the highest rank, else the first picked). The chosen ally must hear you (nearby, or both carrying a communicator); they take one Major action at once, and the commander assists it with Control + Command. Nobody takes more than two Major actions in a round.
Extra actions: point at your character for Extra Minor (1 Momentum, once per turn) or, after your Major action, Second Major (2 Momentum; that task is +1 Difficulty).

Objects in the world (the Power Relay, Alarm Panel, Sensor Console, Damaged Door, Injured Crewmember) work in combat exactly as outside it. Stand within reach, point at your character and pick Interact (or click the object's marker). Each approach shows its cost (Major or Minor) and the full roll before you commit; its effect on the world is immediate.

Move is selected at the start of each turn: click any blue tile to walk there. On a touch screen, tap a blue tile to see the path, then tap it again to walk there. You can Move once per turn, up to your full movement (shown as >> 5/5 above your character); tiles you don't use are lost. You can't Move while a Klingon is right next to you.

Sprint (Major, no roll): point at your acting character and pick Sprint, then click a blue tile. It goes up to twice your movement (shown as +10 beside >> 5/5), once per turn, and never in the same turn as Move. Klingons sprint too. Sprinting is not an attack, so it doesn't spoil an Ambush.
Aim lets you reroll one die on your next attack this turn; with an Accurate weapon (such as a phaser rifle), up to two dice. A focus doesn't change Aim. Aiming twice doesn't give more rerolls.

Assist (Major): click a party member who still has a turn this round, then Assist (or point at your character, pick Assist and choose the ally in the Task panel). Their next task this round (an attack, Guard, First Aid or an object task) rolls your 1d20 as well, against your own Target Number; it adds a success only if they score at least one themselves. One assist per task; unused assists end with the round.

Guard, First Aid, Direct, object tasks, Assist from your own character and a firing mode picked on your own character open in the Task panel on the right: set them up, then press the large yellow button that appears there. Your character's weapon is shown on their party card: click it to switch weapons. Right-click the battlefield to release your selection.
Your turn ends by itself when both actions are used. The End Turn button under the Task panel ends it early.

sections.heading: Attacking
lines: Open the character's action ring and choose Stun or Deadly, then select a target and Fire. Stun incapacitates. Deadly uses lethal force and adds +1 Threat when the attack is committed.
You can also click a Klingon and choose Stun or Deadly next to it to fire at it straight away. The Task panel on the right shows the roll you will make.
The result applies by itself: a hit shows the Injury over the target. If the roll would miss and you have an Aim reroll, it waits so you can reroll a red die or click No Reroll.

Two dice are rolled (up to five with bonus d20s bought in the Task panel). Each die at or under your Target Number (Control + Security for a shot, Daring + Security in melee) is a success; with a focus that fits the weapon, a die at or under your Security is a critical worth 2, and a 1 always is. You need as many successes as the Difficulty. A 20 is a complication.
Difficulty is 2 for a shot (1 in melee), plus 1 for each range band beyond your weapon's best range. A Klingon who sees a melee attack coming defends: its successes set the Difficulty instead.

sections.heading: Cover
lines: Cover is automatic; there is no Take Cover action. Any figure standing right beside a crate or console (on one of its four sides, not a corner) is in cover, and loses it as soon as it moves away.
A blue shield beside a figure's head on the map shows it is in cover. The Target panel shows whether your target is In Cover or has No Cover.
When planning a move, the hint and the Task panel tell you if the route ends in cover. The Klingons use cover the same way.
A target in cover rolls too (Control + Security, with its own focus): if it scores more successes than the Difficulty, the attacker needs that many instead.

sections.heading: Momentum and Threat
lines: Momentum is the away team's shared pool (0-6), the same one used outside combat. Each success beyond the Difficulty adds 1; anything over 6 is lost. Spend it on bonus d20s, 1 to Direct an ally, 1 for an Extra Minor action or 2 for a Second Major action.
Before an attack, buy bonus d20s in the Task panel: the first costs 1, the second 2 more, the third 3 more (5d20 at most). Pay from Momentum, or add the same amount of Threat instead.

Threat is the opposition's pool for the mission. It grows when you make a Deadly attack, when you pay for dice with Threat, and from Momentum the Klingons generate. The Klingons spend it the way you spend Momentum: on bonus d20s, an extra minor action, or a second major action.

sections.heading: Auto Combat (testing)
lines: Auto Combat (bottom right) lets the AI play your party too, with the same rules and dice. Pause, Resume and Stop at any time; Stop hands control back to you. 2x and 4x only make it faster to watch.
Type a Seed on the setup screen to replay the exact same fight. The seed of the current fight is shown in Debug.

Enemy AI picks how the Klingons play, in every fight (not only Auto Combat); Classic is the original enemy AI. Party AI picks how your party plays. Classic acts one action at a time; Turn Planner scores every combination of its Major and Minor action (attack, aim, assist, move, sprint and where it ends up) against the danger of the enemies' next round. To compare them, replay the same Seed with each AI.
